name: Goblincore

card.summary: An internet aesthetic celebrating moss, mushrooms, thrifted clothes and earthy textures, used as a clothing and grooming style built on brown and green palettes and layered secondhand pieces.

quick.overview:
Goblincore is an online aesthetic inspired by goblin folklore that prizes soil, animals, mushrooms and secondhand objects. It grew on Tumblr and TikTok and, per cultural commentators, peaked during the 2020 pandemic.

For looks, it offers a style framework: earth-toned, layered, thrifted clothing, shiny small accessories and a deliberately unpolished grooming approach. The appearance payoff is a distinctive, cohesive personal style with low cost and comfort-oriented pieces.
quick.how: People assemble outfits from thrifted browns, greens and clashing colours, layering textures and adding trinkets such as small jewellery and coins, often with natural motifs like mushrooms and frogs.
quick.risks: As a style trend it carries few risks beyond the cost of impulse purchases; it may be a fleeting fashion.

lead: Goblincore is an internet aesthetic and subculture inspired by goblin folklore that celebrates natural ecosystems and things conventional taste finds unappealing, such as soil, animals and secondhand objects [1]. It is generally thought to have emerged in online communities in the late 2010s, especially on Tumblr and TikTok [1].

The look centres on secondhand clothing, often chosen for comfort, in brown and green and clashing colours, with imagery of frogs, snails, mushrooms, moss and animal skeletons, and collected shiny objects such as silverware, small jewellery and coins [1]. Related names include crowcore, dirtcore, cottagegoth, feralcore, gremlincore and mushroomcore [1].

Coverage included Mashable and Nylon (2020) and Vice, GQ, Refinery29 and The Guardian (2021) [1]. It is often described as a darker companion to cottagecore, which emphasises sunlit fields rather than wild forests [1][2].

chain: Thrifted earth-tone layers and natural-motif accessories
A cohesive, textured, deliberately unpolished outfit
angle.text: Goblincore gives a ready-made wardrobe and accessory vocabulary: layered secondhand pieces in browns and greens, trinkets and nature motifs, assembled into a recognisable look.

paras: Amanda Brennan is cited as saying it began gaining traction in spring 2019 and peaked in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic; by July 2021 the goblincore subreddit had 19,000 subscribers, up 395 percent from July 2020, and Etsy reported a 695 percent increase in related searches in June 2021 [1]. Cottagecore's term dates to Tumblr in 2018 and spread widely in 2020 [2].
Thrifted clothing in brown, green and clashing colours, plus imagery of frogs, snails, earthworms, skeletons, ferns and mushrooms; maximalism and escapism are linked themes [1].

It is described as anti-consumerist, with decor often found or built, and has a notable number of LGBT+ and non-binary proponents with the catchphrase 'no gender, only bugs' [1]. The Guardian described the trend as embracing chaos, dirt and mud [1].

timeline.event: Cottagecore term first appears on Tumblr [2]
Peak during pandemic; press coverage begins [1]
